title: Cocycle for strict-transform charts
statement:
The localized strict-transform chart comparisons agree on double
localizations and satisfy the cocycle equality on triple chart overlaps.

proof.text: Fix a ring map $f:A\to B$, an ideal $I\subseteq A$ and $a\in I$. Write $C_a=B\otimes_A A[I/a]$, $K_a=\Gamma_{(a)}(C_a)$, $R_a=C_a/K_a$, $J=IB$, $b=f(a)$ and $T_a=B[J/b]$. Let $F_a:R_a\to T_a$ be the comparison. First fix this chart and elements $s,t\in R_a$. By [def-nagata-strict-transform-chart-comparison-localized], the two successive localizations of $F_a$, in either order, send an iterated fraction to $F_a(z)F_a(s)^{-m}F_a(t)^{-n}$. After identifying both iterated source rings with $(R_a)_{st}$ and both iterated target rings with $(T_a)_{F_a(st)}$, the two maps therefore agree. The inverses exist because inverting a product inverts each factor (an inverse of $s$ is $t(st)^{-1}$). Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property] proves equality of the maps, not just of their presentations. For $s_0,t_0\in B$, take $s,t$ to be their structural images in $R_a$. Then [lemma-nagata-strict-transform-chart-localization-data] identifies successive quotient-chart localizations with the chart of localized data, and [lemma-nagata-strict-transform-chart-localization] identifies the maps with the comparisons constructed there. For elements of $A$, apply this assertion to their images in $B$. The coefficient-chart identifications themselves agree by [lemma-nagata-affine-blowup-restrict-cocycle].

source.place: Proof, compatibility with localized data and double localizations; expanded using Stacks Tag 00CP

proof.text:
Now let $a,a'\in I$ and put $u=1\otimes(a'/a)\in C_a$, $v=1\otimes(a/a')\in C_{a'}$. The map of [def-nagata-homogeneous-away-to-chart] sends $xt^n/(at)^n$ to $x/a^n$; [lemma-nagata-homogeneous-away-to-chart], [lemma-nagata-homogeneous-away-to-chart-injective] and [lemma-nagata-homogeneous-away-to-chart-surjective] make it a ring isomorphism. Use this to identify the degree-zero Rees chart with $A[I/a]$. Apply [lemma-nagata-proj-chart-ring-cocycle] to the degree-one elements $aX,a'X$ of the Rees algebra: it gives the ordinary transition between the localized chart rings on their intersection. Extending this transition by the identity on $B$ gives
$$\theta_{aa'}:(C_a)_u\xrightarrow{\sim}(C_{a'})_v.$$
Here [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-localization-away-base-change] identifies localizing the tensor chart with tensoring the localized chart, and [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] gives the extended map and its inverse. The fraction description of [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring] gives its explicit formula: it fixes $B$ and sends $x/a$ to $(x/a')v^{-1}$ for $x\in I$, so it sends $u$ to $v^{-1}$. In the common overlap ring the structural images satisfy $a'=au$, with $u$ a unit. No cancellation of $a$ is being asserted in $C_a$: this relation already holds in $A[I/a]\subseteq A_a$ and is preserved by tensoring. For three indices the extended ordinary transitions satisfy $\theta_{a'a''}\theta_{aa'}=\theta_{aa''}$ after further localization: this is the cited Proj cocycle, extended on pure tensors by $y\otimes z\mapsto y\otimes\theta(z)$.

proof.text:
The quotient rings really restrict to the quotients of the overlap rings. For any $c\in C_a$, the extension $K_a(C_a)_c$ equals the $a/1$-power-torsion ideal of $(C_a)_c$. Indeed, if $a^n(z/c^m)=0$, the localization relation says $c^ka^nz=0$ for some $k\geq0$; hence $c^kz\in K_a$ and $z/c^m=(c^kz)/c^{m+k}$ belongs to the extended ideal. Conversely a fraction with numerator killed by $a^n$ is killed by the same power after localization; finite sums use the maximum of the exponents. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-quotient-commute] we consequently have
$$(R_a)_{\bar c}\cong (C_a)_c/\Gamma_{(a/1)}((C_a)_c),\qquad [z]/\bar c^m\longmapsto[z/c^m].$$
The torsion ideal here is precisely the one defined in [def-nagata-strict-transform-chart-ring]. This argument applies to chart elements such as $u$, not merely to images of elements of $B$.

source.place: Tag 00CT, proposition-localize-quotient; the power-torsion calculation is an explicit fraction argument supplementing Tag 0BIP, lemma-blowup-base-change

proof.text:
In the ordinary overlap of step 2, $a'=au$ with $u$ invertible. Thus $a^nz=0$ if and only if $(a')^nz=u^na^nz=0$: the reverse implication multiplies by $u^{-n}$. Since $\theta_{aa'}$ fixes structural scalars, it therefore carries the $a$-power-torsion ideal exactly onto the $a'$-power-torsion ideal. Using step 3, define
$$\bar\theta_{aa'}:(R_a)_{\bar u}\longrightarrow(R_{a'})_{\bar v},\qquad [w]\longmapsto[\theta_{aa'}(w)].$$
If $w-w'$ is in the source ideal then its image is in the target ideal, so this formula is well-defined and respects sums, products and $1$. The inverse is induced by $\theta_{aa'}^{-1}$. Every quotient class has a representative, so the displayed commutation with the quotient maps characterizes $\bar\theta_{aa'}$ uniquely. This is descent of a map through a surjective quotient as in [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], with the ideals identified in [def-nagata-strict-transform-chart-ring].

source.place: Tag 0BIP, lemma-blowup-base-change, quotient chart description; explicit descent on representatives

proof.text:
Check that these descended transitions are compatible with the comparisons named in the statement. Apply the ordinary transition construction also to the charts $T_a=B[J/b]$ and $T_{a'}=B[J/f(a')]$, using [lemma-nagata-proj-chart-ring-cocycle] over $B$; denote it by $\tau_{aa'}$. In its target overlap put $v_B=b/f(a')$. By [def-nagata-strict-chart-to-extended-blowup-chart], the unquotiented comparison $\sigma_a$ fixes $B$ and sends $x/a$ to $f(x)/b$. The two routes from the $a$-chart to the target overlap agree on $B$ and on every generator $x/a$, since both have value
$$\frac{f(x)}{f(a')}v_B^{-1}.$$
They also agree on the inverted $u$, whose image is $v_B^{-1}$. The blowup chart is generated by the $x/a$ over $A$ [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]; tensor uniqueness and localization uniqueness therefore give equality on the whole overlap. The quotient comparison [def-nagata-strict-transform-chart-comparison] satisfies $F_aq_a=\sigma_a$. Surjectivity of the overlap quotient then gives
$$\tau_{aa'}\circ(F_a)_{\bar u}=(F_{a'})_{\bar v}\circ\bar\theta_{aa'}.$$
These localized maps are exactly those of [def-nagata-strict-transform-chart-comparison-localized], by their fraction formula. Together with step 1 this checks the comparisons for base-localized presentations too.

blueprint_notes.label: status
blueprint_notes.text:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the strict transform is
supplied by the API of
`WeilConjectures/Compactification/StrictTransform.lean` —
`AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransform`, its closed immersion
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.isClosedImmersion_pullbackLift_blowup_comap`,
and the pullback square
`AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_strictTransformOpen` — so the
strict-transform chart rings and their cocycle are never assembled by hand.

blueprint_update.statement:
The localized strict-transform chart comparisons agree on double
localizations and satisfy the cocycle equality on triple chart overlaps.

proof.text:
On an intersection of the $a$- and $a'$-charts, choose a basic affine
refinement on which both chart restrictions are defined. The ordinary
blow-up transition is the specified localization isomorphism; by
[lemma-nagata-affine-blowup-restrict-cocycle] its two composites on a
triple refinement agree. Localizing the quotient map
$C_a\twoheadrightarrow C_a^{\mathrm{st}}$ gives the quotient by the
localized power-torsion ideal, by
[lemma-nagata-strict-transform-chart-localization-data]. Thus the
ordinary transition descends uniquely to a transition of strict-transform
chart rings. The descended maps agree with the comparisons constructed
after localization by
[lemma-nagata-strict-transform-chart-localization]. On a triple
refinement their two composites become the same ordinary transition before
quotienting, hence are equal after quotienting. This proves both the
double-overlap compatibility and the cocycle.
